news.title: FA chair urges FIFA president to release documents over controversial World Cup plan
news.lede: London, Sepr.17 (SANA) Football Association (FA) chair Debbie Hewitt has called on FIFA President Gianni Infantino to release all documents related to his abandoned plan to sell a stake in a new commercial company managing World Cup and other tournament rights. In a letter sent to Infantino and FIFA Secretary General Mattias Grafström, Hewitt, who is also a FIFA vice-president, requested that the FIFA Council receive a written explanation for the decision to suspend the one-match ban imposed on US forward Folarin Balogun during the World Cup. Hewitt asked FIFA to make the documents available before the next FIFA Council meeting scheduled for Oct. 15, citing concerns over governance and the organisation’s internal culture. Scrapped commercial proposal sparks controversy.

news.title: Tunisia star retires from international football after three World Cup appearances
news.lede: Cologne star Ellyes Skhiri has called time on his international career with Tunisia. Skhiri broke the news on his Instagram account: "The moment has come for me to announce the end of my international career." "Wearing this shirt and representing my homeland was a source of immense pride and honour," he added. "The emotions, the moments of participation, and all these memories will remain engraved in my mind."

news.title: FA chief demands full Fifa probe into Gianni Infantino's World Cup sell plot & Donald Trump's secret call to unban star
news.lede: FA CHAIR Debbie Hewitt wants Gianni Infantino to release all the documents concerning his radical plan to flog stakes in the World Cup. Hewitt, 63, wrote a letter to the Fifa president this week and it was also sent to the governing body’s secretary general Mattias Grafstrom. The Fifa Council are due to meet next month and Hewitt believes all members should have the files relating to Infantino’s scheme before then. She has also called for an explanation over the decision to suspend USA striker Folarin Balogun’s ban at this summer’s World Cup.

news.title: This college football team just adopted the World Cup's most viral chant — keeping Norway's Viking Row alive
news.lede: Norway's Viking Row was one of the most viral fan traditions of the 2026 World Cup. Now, two months later, it has officially made its way into American college football. The University of Minnesota debuted its own version of the synchronized rowing chant at its season opener at Huntington Bank Stadium, with the student section sitting in rows and mimicking the same exaggerated rowing motion that Norwegian fans made famous this summer. Former Gophers linebacker Kamal Martin led the chant before kickoff.

news.title: FA chair Hewitt demands Infantino release records of failed World Cup plan
news.lede: Letter sent before Fifa council meeting on 15 October. Infantino under pressure before presidential election. The Football Association’s chair, Debbie Hewitt, has written to Gianni Infantino demanding that Fifa releases all documents relating to his abandoned World Cup sell-off plan and the decision to lift the USA striker Folarin Balogun’s suspension during last summer’s tournament. The Guardian revealed last month that Hewitt and other members of the Fifa council were lobbying for an independent review of the proposed Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) sell-off and the Balogun controversy.

news.title: Soccer-FA's Hewitt asks Infantino to release records on World Cup plan, Balogun suspension
news.lede: Sept 17 (Reuters) - England ⁠FA chair and FIFA vice-president Debbie Hewitt has ⁠written to FIFA President Gianni Infantino seeking the ‌release of material related to his abandoned World Cup investment plan and the lifting of U.S. striker Folarin Balogun's suspension, an FA ​source confirmed to Reuters on Thursday. Infantino, ⁠56, has been under ⁠mounting pressure since unveiling a proposal to sell a commercial ⁠stake ‌in the World Cup to private investors. The plan sparked fierce opposition, with UEFA, the Asian ⁠Football Confederation and North America's CONCACAF among ​those calling for ‌changes at the top of FIFA. Balogun was handed ⁠a one-match ​ban at the 2026 World Cup after receiving a red card in his side's 2-0 round-of-32 win over Bosnia ⁠and Herzegovina that would have ruled ​him out of their last-16 clash with Belgium.
